schema_ddl:
CREATE TABLE EMPLOYEE (
    EMPID INT,
    NAME VARCHAR(255),
    SUPERVISOR INT,
    SALARY INT,
    PRIMARY KEY (EMPID),
    CHECK (EMPID <> SUPERVISOR),
    CHECK (SALARY >= 0)
);

CREATE TABLE BONUS (
    EMPID INT,
    BONUS INT,
    PRIMARY KEY (EMPID),
    FOREIGN KEY (EMPID) REFERENCES EMPLOYEE(EMPID),
    CHECK (BONUS >= 0)
);
q1: SELECT EMPLOYEE.NAME, BONUS.BONUS FROM EMPLOYEE LEFT JOIN BONUS ON EMPLOYEE.EMPID = BONUS.EMPID WHERE BONUS < 1000 OR BONUS IS NULL
q2: SELECT EMPLOYEE.NAME, BONUS.BONUS FROM EMPLOYEE LEFT JOIN BONUS ON EMPLOYEE.EMPID = BONUS.EMPID WHERE COALESCE(BONUS,0) <1000

q2_prompt_sql: SELECT EMPLOYEE.NAME, BONUS.BONUS FROM EMPLOYEE LEFT JOIN BONUS ON EMPLOYEE.EMPID = BONUS.EMPID WHERE COALESCE(BONUS,0) <1000
counterexample: INSERT INTO EMPLOYEE (EMPID, NAME, SUPERVISOR, SALARY) VALUES (1, 'John Doe', 2, 5000); INSERT INTO BONUS (EMPID, BONUS) VALUES (1, NULL);
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent because they handle NULL values differently in the WHERE clause. Q1 explicitly checks for NULL values in the BONUS column, while Q2 uses the COALESCE function to treat NULL as 0 for the comparison.
counterexample_dsp: The difference is triggered when an employee has a NULL bonus value. In Q1, this employee will be included in the result, but in Q2, they will not.
